items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: The transcript identifies Monk Rowe as the interviewer ('My name is Monk Rowe... have Chico Hamilton with me'). There is no narrative content describing a personal or professional relationship between Chico Hamilton and Monk Rowe beyond the interview context.

ctx.x: Chico was interviewed in Los Angeles on January 30, 2000, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming in Manhattan today, and I’m very, very pleased to have Chico Hamilton with me, who has had a long, illustrious and varied career in music. Would you mind telling me what you’re up to in the year 2000?

Sure. I’m just trying to stay alive. No, as a matter of fact we’re up to a whole lot of things. The group, my orchestra — I don’t refer to it as a band, it’s an orchestra, because I think we try to cover all facets of music, not just one direction you know, and not just necessarily under the terminology of even jazz — J-A-Z-Z. I really disapprove of the word myself. I’m in complete accordance with people, with Duke Ellington, Miles Davis, people like that. Why not call it just my music, Chico’s music? Duke…
